name: Propylthiouracil
route_note: oral tablet in divided doses two to three times daily

discovery.by: Edwin Astwood and colleagues, Tufts / Harvard
discovery.note: Identified among thiouracil derivatives as more potent and less toxic than thiouracil.

tagline: Antithyroid drug kept for early pregnancy and thyroid storm because of liver risk
summary: Propylthiouracil is a thionamide that blocks thyroid hormone synthesis and also inhibits peripheral conversion of T4 to T3. Because of a risk of severe liver injury it is now reserved mainly for the first trimester of pregnancy, thyroid storm and patients who cannot take methimazole.
mechanism: Like methimazole, PTU inhibits thyroid peroxidase, reducing iodination of thyroglobulin and coupling of iodotyrosines, so new T4 and T3 synthesis falls over weeks.
PTU additionally inhibits type 1 5'-deiodinase in peripheral tissues, reducing conversion of T4 to the more active T3; this rapid effect is the rationale for its use in thyroid storm.
uses: Hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease, toxic multinodular goitre) in patients intolerant of methimazole
Hyperthyroidism during the first trimester of pregnancy

history.title: PTU identified
history.detail: Propylthiouracil is reported as a more potent, better-tolerated derivative.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: PTU becomes available in the US.

history.title: Liver safety review
history.detail: FDA and the American Thyroid Association highlight cases of PTU-associated liver failure and transplants, including in children.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning on severe liver injury and acute liver failure.

serious: severe hepatotoxicity and acute liver failure
safety.boxed_warning: Severe liver injury and acute liver failure, some fatal or requiring transplant; reserve for patients who cannot tolerate methimazole or when surgery/radioiodine are unsuitable; preferred in first trimester of pregnancy.

facts: PTU is preferred in the first trimester because methimazole is associated with a specific embryopathy.
Its short half-life requires dosing several times a day.
